: comparable to C/C++; no runtime, no GC.
: no null pointers, no dangling pointers, no buffer overflows.
: iterators, traits, generics compile down to the same machine code you'd write by hand.
: algebraic data types (enums), pattern matching, traits.

Rust moves correctness checks to compile time. A program that compiles is far more likely to "just work" than in most languages. The cost: longer compile times and a steeper learning curve (especially ownership/lifetimes).
